rules.title: Allowable Annual Rent Increase - Oakland Rent Adjustment Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered rental units in Oakland can only raise rent once every 12 months, based on the annual CPI rate, and total rent increases cannot exceed 10% in a year.
rules.key_value: CPI rate (2.3% for Aug 2024-Jul 2025); capped at 10%
rules.coverage_conditions: Covered rental units under the Oakland Rent Adjustment Ordinance (O.M.C. 8.22.070 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: Tenants can be given only one rent increase in any 12-month period. An increase cannot happen earlier than 12 months after a tenant’s move-in date or 12 months after the last rent increase.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is a 'covered rental unit' under the Rent Adjustment Ordinance

rules.conflict_note: The text references both a local 10% cap and a 'state cap' of 9.2% (8.8% for Aug 2024-Jul 2025) that applies when combined with a RAP-approved petition increase; relationship between the two caps is not fully specified.

rules.title: State rent increase notice and cap reference (Ca. Civ. Code § 827 / state cap)
rules.requirement: California law requires 30 days' advance written notice for rent increases up to 10%, and sets a state rent increase cap (noted as currently 9.2%, with 8.8% applicable Aug 2024-Jul 2025) for units covered by state law, yielding to stricter local rent control where applicable.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered under California state rent cap law (not covered by stricter local rent control ordinances such as Oakland's)
rules.quoted_span: California law requires that tenants be provided with 30 days' advance written notice of rent increases up to 10% (Ca. Civ. Code § 827).
rules.conflict_note: Text mixes a 30-days-notice threshold tied to a 10% increase with a separately stated 'state cap' figure of 9.2%/8.8%, which appears to reference Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12's statewide rent cap rather than § 827 itself; some ambiguity in how these interact.
